item.text: The two failures trace to `config.GetEOL`: Ubuntu 20.04 has only a standard support date, and 22.04 has no map entry. `ScanResult.CheckEOL` uses that lookup to report both support status and unknown releases. I’m adding a focused regression test for the dates and support transitions before changing the map.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat >> .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'

Investigation: "'`config.GetEOL` maps Ubuntu releases by exact version. Its 20.04 entry lacks `ExtendedSupportUntil`; `IsExtendedSuppportEnded` then falls back to the standard date. The 22.04 key is absent, so `CheckEOL` reports unknown release. Existing 18.04 entry demonstrates both date fields, and `ScanResult.CheckEOL` consumes the same lookup.
Hypothesis: Adding the two specified metadata entries will correct support transitions and release recognition without changing detection or warning logic.
EOF'

item.text:
Updated [Ubuntu lifecycle data](/app/config/os.go:137) so 20.04 has extended support through April 1, 2030, and 22.04 is recognized with standard support through April 1, 2027 and extended support through April 1, 2032. Added a [regression test](/app/config/os_test.go:10) for both releases and their support boundaries.

The config, models, and scanner tests passed.
